domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee's application for leave. Tracks the full lifecycle from draft through approval/rejection to cancellation. On approval, triggers balance deduction.
lifecycle_states: DRAFT — initial state; employee is composing the request but has not yet submitted it for review
SUBMITTED — employee has submitted the request; pending manager action
APPROVED — manager has approved the request; balance has been deducted; terminal (unless cancelled)
REJECTED — manager has rejected the request; no balance impact; terminal
CANCELLED — request has been withdrawn or cancelled; can be reached from DRAFT, SUBMITTED, or APPROVED; if cancelled from APPROVED, balance is restored

domain_entities.name: LeaveType
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of leave categories. Each type maps to a distinct LeavePolicy that governs entitlement, accrual, and approval rules.

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines the rules governing a specific leave type: how many days are entitled, whether approval is required, minimum notice period, and accrual/accumulation caps.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — policy is in effect; leave requests can reference this policy
INACTIVE — policy has been retired; no new leave requests may reference it, but historical data remains

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: Tracks an employee's leave entitlement, consumption, and remaining balance for a specific LeavePolicy within a fiscal year. RemainingDays is derived: totalEntitlement - usedDays. Status reflects availability.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — balance is available for leave requests; remainingDays > 0
EXHAUSTED — remainingDays = 0; no further leave of this type can be approved until entitlement resets or accrues
FROZEN — balance is temporarily unavailable (e.g., employee suspended or on long-term unpaid leave); no deductions or requests allowed

domain_entities.name: LeaveRequestStatus
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of lifecycle states for a LeaveRequest. Governs which transitions are legal and which actor may perform them.

business_rules: A LeaveRequest's startDate must be on or before its endDate. Violation prevents submission. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

The number of leave days consumed by a request is computed as: (endDate - startDate) + 1, counting calendar days inclusively. This count is used for balance sufficiency checks and for deducting usedDays on approval. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance appears, not only here]

Before a LeaveRequest transitions to APPROVED, the employee's LeaveBalance for the corresponding policy and fiscal year must have remainingDays >= the requested day count. If insufficient, the request must be REJECTED. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance appears, not only here]

When a LeaveRequest transitions to APPROVED, the corresponding LeaveBalance.usedDays is incremented by the request's day count, and remainingDays is recalculated. If remainingDays reaches 0, the balance status transitions to EXHAUSTED. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance appears, not only here]

When a LeaveRequest transitions from APPROVED to CANCELLED, the corresponding LeaveBalance.usedDays is decremented by the request's day count, and remainingDays is recalculated. If the balance was EXHAUSTED, it returns to ACTIVE. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance appears, not only here]

If the LeavePolicy referenced by a LeaveRequest has requiresManagerApproval = true, the request must be approved by the employee's manager (Employee.managerId). If requiresManagerApproval = false, the request auto-approves on submission (DRAFT → SUBMITTED → APPROVED in a single logical transition). [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeavePolicy appears, not only here]

If the LeavePolicy has a minimumNoticeDays value, the LeaveRequest's startDate must be at least minimumNoticeDays after the submission date. The notice period is measured in calendar days from the submission timestamp (not the start of the submission day). Violation prevents submission. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeavePolicy appears, not only here]

Only the employee who owns the request (employeeId) may submit a DRAFT. Only the employee's manager (Employee.managerId) may approve or reject a SUBMITTED request. Only the owning employee may cancel a request in DRAFT or SUBMITTED state. Cancellation from APPROVED requires manager action. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

A LeaveRequest in DRAFT state may be edited freely by the owning employee. Once SUBMITTED, only the status field may change (to APPROVED, REJECTED, or CANCELLED) — no field edits are allowed. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]
A LeaveRequest cannot be submitted if the employee's employment status is INACTIVE or TERMINATED. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

The fiscal year for a LeaveRequest is determined by the calendar year of its startDate. The corresponding LeaveBalance is matched on (employeeId, policyId, fiscalYear). If no balance record exists for that fiscal year, one must be created with totalEntitlement from the LeavePolicy before the request can be approved. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance appears, not only here]

Overlapping leave requests for the same employee are not allowed. A new LeaveRequest cannot be submitted (or approved) if its date range [startDate, endDate] overlaps with any existing APPROVED or SUBMITTED request for the same employee. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

A manager cannot approve or reject their own leave request. If the employee has no manager (managerId is null) and the policy requires approval, the request must be escalated or auto-rejected based on organizational policy. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]
domain_notes:
## Lifecycle states introduced (for architectureMdUpdate)

### LeaveRequest
- **DRAFT** — employee is composing; editable; not yet submitted
- **SUBMITTED** — pending manager review; immutable except status
- **APPROVED** — terminal (unless cancelled); balance deducted
- **REJECTED** — terminal; no balance impact
- **CANCELLED** — withdrawn; reachable from DRAFT, SUBMITTED, or APPROVED; if from APPROVED, balance restored

### LeavePolicy
- **ACTIVE** — in effect; new requests can reference it
- **INACTIVE** — retired; historical data only

### LeaveBalance
- **ACTIVE** — remainingDays > 0; available for requests
- **EXHAUSTED** — remainingDays = 0; no further approvals
- **FROZEN** — temporarily unavailable (e.g., employee suspended)

### Key state transition rules
- DRAFT → SUBMITTED: employee only; requires ACTIVE employment status; minimumNoticeDays enforced; no overlapping SUBMITTED/APPROVED requests
- SUBMITTED → APPROVED: manager only (not self); balance sufficiency checked; balance deducted; if requiresManagerApproval=false, auto-approves
- SUBMITTED → REJECTED: manager only (not self); no balance impact
- DRAFT/SUBMITTED → CANCELLED: employee only
- APPROVED → CANCELLED: manager only; balance restored
- Balance ACTIVE → EXHAUSTED: automatic when remainingDays hits 0 after deduction
- Balance EXHAUSTED → ACTIVE: automatic when remainingDays > 0 after restoration

### Foundational semantics (broad scope)
- Day count: (endDate - startDate) + 1, calendar days inclusive — used everywhere (sufficiency check, deduction, restoration)
- Fiscal year: derived from calendar year of startDate; balance matched on (employeeId, policyId, fiscalYear)
- Overlap detection: [startDate, endDate] inclusive range against all SUBMITTED/APPROVED requests for same employee

open_questions.question: Should leave day counting use calendar days or business days (excluding weekends and/or public holidays)?
open_questions.impact: Affects balance deduction amounts, sufficiency checks, and entitlement calculations. Calendar days are simpler but may over-count for office-based leave. Business days require a holiday calendar and weekend exclusion logic.
candidate_options: Business days: exclude Saturdays and Sundays
Business days with holidays: exclude weekends plus a configurable holiday calendar

open_questions.question: Should the minimum notice period be measured from the submission timestamp or from the start of the submission day (midnight)?
open_questions.impact: Affects whether an employee can submit a leave request late in the day for a leave starting exactly minimumNoticeDays later. Timestamp-based is stricter; midnight-based is more employee-friendly.
candidate_options: From start of submission day (midnight, more lenient)

open_questions.question: Should the fiscal year follow the calendar year (Jan 1 – Dec 31) or a configurable company fiscal year (e.g., Apr 1 – Mar 31)?
open_questions.impact: Determines which LeaveBalance record a request maps to and when entitlements reset. A configurable fiscal year adds complexity but is necessary for organizations with non-calendar fiscal years.
candidate_options: Configurable fiscal year start month per organization

open_questions.question: What happens when an employee has no manager (managerId is null) but the leave policy requires approval?
open_questions.impact: Determines the escalation path. Options: auto-approve (risky), auto-reject (harsh), escalate to a default approver (e.g., HR admin), or block submission until a manager is assigned.
candidate_options: Escalate to a designated HR/admin role
Block submission until manager is assigned
